minutes.headline: Planning Board reworked draft subdivision rules, struck the sewer-connection mandate, and agreed to hold a hearing on full-size plans.
minutes.summary: The Planning Board met remotely, heard committee reports and a cannabis community meeting announcement, then reviewed the draft definitive subdivision rules section by section. Members struck the requirement to connect to town sewer and agreed to schedule a hearing to require full-size plan sets. A late discussion covered the Orion subdivision's possible water connection and the need for a modification.

decisions.decision: Strike the sentence requiring subdivisions to connect to town sewer, keeping the sentence that lots not served by town sewer need an approved disposal system.
Revise the percolation test provision to require showing the location and results of any tests conducted on the plan.
List the departments for the pre-construction conference: police, fire, conservation commission, DPW, water district, planning, and board of health.
Director to schedule a public hearing to change the rules and regulations from 11 by 17 plan copies to full-size plan sets for the board.

Next meetings set for February 8 and February 22.

what_happened.line: The board agreed to strike the sentence requiring subdivisions to connect to town sewer, keeping the rule that lots without town sewer need an approved disposal system.
The director is to schedule a public hearing to change the rules from 11 by 17 plan copies to full-size plan sets for the board.
Until then, applicants will be asked to provide larger plan sets voluntarily.
If the water district approves a water connection for the Orion subdivision, the applicant will be told to seek a modification, after the director checks with town counsel.
The board heard that the capital committee ranked the fiscal 22 capital requests and the town manager recommended funding the top group within available funds.

why_it_matters: The subdivision rules decide what developers must build and submit in town, including whether new lots must tie into town sewer or use on-site disposal, so the draft changes shape future development.
A water line added to the Orion subdivision would enter the cost estimate behind the surety held to guarantee the work, which bears on whether the town is protected if the work is not finished.
The fiscal 22 capital plan funds only part of the ranked requests, so some projects may come before voters later or wait.
